Check: Record endpoint; tenant; site; agent; installer; enrollment; and impact
Evidence to capture: Customer; site; hostname; durable device ID; agent version; installer source; first failure
Likely cause: Wrong scope; stale installer; deployment mismatch
Safe next action: Preserve context before retrying

Check: Capture the exact certificate or TLS error
Evidence to capture: Error text; code; destination; port; protocol; service state; logs; events
Likely cause: Handshake; trust; name; expiry; revocation; proxy; policy failure
Safe next action: Retain original evidence and first error
Escalation trigger: Error indicates suspicious certificate or credential exposure

Check: Determine the affected cohort
Evidence to capture: Count; endpoint image; site; network; proxy; OS; agent version; customer
Likely cause: Shared image; network path; version; tenant; service incident
Safe next action: Group by common attributes before repair
Escalation trigger: Multiple customers or regions are affected

Check: Correlate recent changes
Evidence to capture: Deployment; token; certificate; trust; proxy; firewall; inspection; hardening events
Likely cause: Recent rotation; policy; route; or package change
Safe next action: Identify the first change aligned to failure

Check: Verify date; time; zone; source; and drift
Evidence to capture: Local and reference time; W32Time state; correction events
Likely cause: Clock skew; bad snapshot; failed synchronization
Safe next action: Restore approved time synchronization

Check: Resolve the documented service hostname
Evidence to capture: Resolver; addresses; route; proxy; destination; port; result
Likely cause: DNS; routing; proxy; firewall; stale endpoint list
Safe next action: Correct the narrow verified dependency
Escalation trigger: Unknown destination or broad bypass proposed

Check: Compare with a working peer
Evidence to capture: DNS; route; proxy; trust; policy; version differences
Likely cause: Endpoint-specific or cohort-specific configuration drift
Safe next action: Change one verified difference on a canary

Check: Separate vendor service from local path
Evidence to capture: Vendor status; alternate approved path; observation times
Likely cause: Vendor outage; regional issue; local site failure
Safe next action: Follow service incident or local-path procedure

Check: Capture the presented certificate and chain
Evidence to capture: Subject; SAN; issuer; serial; validity; thumbprint; key usage; chain
Likely cause: Wrong certificate; proxy substitution; incomplete chain
Safe next action: Compare against documented service identity

Check: Verify name and chain in the service context
Evidence to capture: Requested hostname; chain result; trusted root; service identity
Likely cause: Name mismatch; missing intermediate; untrusted root
Safe next action: Repair trust through approved vendor or enterprise path

Check: Test revocation and intermediate retrieval
Evidence to capture: CRL or OCSP result; AIA result; URLs; chain-build code
Likely cause: Blocked revocation; unavailable intermediate; offline cache
Safe next action: Restore documented retrieval path

Check: Review Schannel and agent evidence
Evidence to capture: Event IDs; alert; error code; process; timestamp; correlation
Likely cause: Protocol; cipher; signature; certificate; trust; handshake failure
Safe next action: Map the first failure to the affected layer
Escalation trigger: Security policy or certificate appears compromised

Check: Identify path-changing security controls
Evidence to capture: Proxy; SWG; inspection; VPN; EDR; content filter; route
Likely cause: TLS inspection; quarantine; redirected traffic
Safe next action: Confirm expected policy and ownership

Check: Compare issuer and thumbprint by path
Evidence to capture: Failing and working certificate chains; inspection root
Likely cause: Stale inspection root; inconsistent policy; bypass path
Safe next action: Repair the intended scoped trust path

Check: Review protocol and cryptographic policy
Evidence to capture: TLS versions; cipher policy; FIPS; hardening; application-control events
Likely cause: Unsupported protocol; recent hardening; blocked binary
Safe next action: Use supported policy and vendor requirements

Check: Reject broad security bypasses
Evidence to capture: Requested exception; destinations; owner; duration; approval
Likely cause: Pressure to disable validation or protection
Safe next action: Use documented destinations and a narrow time-bounded exception
Escalation trigger: Global TLS; revocation; inspection; or EDR disablement

Check: Match token; installer; tenant; site; region; and device
Evidence to capture: Token issuance; package source; tenant; site; region; device ID
Likely cause: Wrong tenant; stale token; copied package; region mismatch
Safe next action: Issue a current authorized enrollment package

Check: Check expiry; revocation; rotation; and use state
Evidence to capture: Token age; certificate dates; revocation; rotation; consumption
Likely cause: Expired or revoked enrollment material
Safe next action: Use vendor-supported renewal or repair

Check: Search for cloned or stale identities
Evidence to capture: Agent ID; hostname; serial; image history; snapshot; uninstall; records
Likely cause: Golden-image capture; reimage; rollback; incomplete uninstall
Safe next action: Contain automation and reconcile identities
Escalation trigger: Two active privileged records share one identity

Check: Use supported renewal or clean re-enrollment
Evidence to capture: Repair method; authorization; old and new IDs; removal evidence
Likely cause: Damaged registration or certificate state
Safe next action: Repair one canary and preserve identity mapping
Escalation trigger: Vendor repair changes tenant or creates duplicates

Check: Repair the verified dependency on one canary
Evidence to capture: Cause; change; actor; time; output; rollback; stop condition
Likely cause: Unbounded or multi-variable remediation
Safe next action: Change one verified dependency and retest

Check: Verify full enrollment and check-in evidence
Evidence to capture: Clock; path; chain; identity; service; heartbeat; inventory; audit event
Likely cause: Partial repair; stale console; identity mismatch
Safe next action: Wait documented interval and re-evaluate current evidence

Check: Test privileged functions separately
Evidence to capture: Monitoring; bounded script; patch scan; remote-support authorization; audit evidence
Likely cause: Heartbeat recovered but modules remain broken
Safe next action: Open owned work for each failed function

Check: Reconcile cohort and prevent recurrence
Evidence to capture: Recovered; failed; duplicate; stale; revoked; excluded; unknown; owner; review
Likely cause: Hidden residual failures; weak image or rotation process
Safe next action: Update deployment; trust; image; and monitoring runbooks
